newsitem.title: USA: Brent still lurks on US Gulf Coast, arb narrows.
newsitem.headline: Brent still lurks on US Gulf Coast, arb narrows.

text.p: North Sea Brent still lurked on the U.S. Gulf Coast on Thursday despite the narrowing transatlantic arbitrage, traders said.

The spread between benchmarks West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and Brent for April was around 75-80 cents a barrel Thursday afternoon, a level which probably precludes sellers from making money directly off of Brent sales into the Gulf.
Nonetheless, Swiss-based trader Glencore was heard to have sold four Brent cargoes since last week into the U.S..
Glencore may have a paper position that it is trying to protect with the sales, traders said.
The last deal was heard done at May WTI minus 80-90 cents a barrel for first-half April.
One Gulf Coast refiner said the trading house was talking about bringing over additional Brent cargoes for later in April, but this could not be confirmed.

West African cargoes remain plentiful. A top Wall Street firm was heard offering a Cabinda at May WTI minus $1.00 a barrel for April 5-10, but this price was deemed to be 40 or 50 cents over the mark.

In Latin America, Ecuador's state oil company Petroecuador declared force majeure on Oriente cargoes loading in March after a pump on the main Transecuadoran pipeline exploded March 7, a company official said.
Pumping operations returned to normal on March 12, and the declaration is likely to be lifted in the next day or two.
Eight to 10 cargoes out of the normal monthly allotment of around 20 will probably be affected, the official said.
Petroecuador notified customers that it will guarantee a minimum of 360,000 barrels per cargo for the month.
Elsewhere, Chile's state oil company ENAP bought 950,000 barrels of Forcados and 360,000 barrels of Oriente from Swiss-based trader Glencore for April 10-14 delivery, trade sources said.
The Nigerian crude was sold on a dated-related basis, while the Oriente was priced off of WTI/Cushing.
Meanwhile, Uruguay's state oil company ANCAP bought around one million barrels of Suez Blend crude from a U.S. major for May 12-14 delivery.
The price was related to dated Brent.
From Colombia, a half cargo of Cano Limon loading in March is still looking for a home, relfecting the increasingly crowded field for short-haul imports into the Gulf.
